title: Layer-uniform fluctuation law: rel_k ~ c(k) K/N, linear in k
law: rel_k grows LINEARLY in k at fixed N (no factorial growth): rel_k ~ c(k) K/N with c(k) ~ k/2 — every FIXED layer decays as K/N -> 0
significance: refutes the exponential-moment-error fear at the fluctuation level: the naive T8-style exp growth (C^r/m) does NOT appear in the cross-q fluctuation; all layers are uniformly K/N-controlled. The obstacle to higher layers is COMPUTATIONAL (variety dimension), not analytic.
